scale.1: Strong concern: significant gaps; would not pass this dimension at the target level.
scale.2: Below bar: partially demonstrated, needed substantial help, or had notable errors.
scale.3: At bar: solid, with minor gaps; meets FAANG mid/senior expectations.
scale.4: Above bar: exceptional, independent, insightful, and polished.

dimensions.name: Problem understanding & approach
dimensions.signals: Asked clarifying questions about inputs, constraints, and edge cases before coding; stated a brute-force baseline; reasoned toward a better approach; compared alternatives; made deliberate decisions instead of guessing.

levels.1: Started coding without understanding the problem; could not produce a working approach even with hints.
levels.2: Reached an approach only with significant hints; little exploration of alternatives.
levels.3: Clarified the problem, found an efficient approach with at most light nudges, and explained why it works.
levels.4: Quickly identified the core insight, compared multiple approaches with tradeoffs, and anticipated follow-ups.

dimensions.name: Algorithms & complexity
dimensions.signals: Chose appropriate data structures; reached the optimal or near-optimal complexity; stated time and space complexity correctly and justified it.

levels.1: Inefficient solution with incorrect or missing complexity analysis.
levels.2: Working but sub-optimal solution, or optimal but with shaky or incorrect analysis.
levels.3: Optimal or near-optimal solution with a correct complexity analysis.
levels.4: Optimal solution, precise analysis including tradeoffs and lower bounds, and awareness of constant factors.

dimensions.name: Coding & correctness
dimensions.signals: Code compiles or runs and passes the hidden tests; readable naming and structure; idiomatic use of the language; no needless complexity; handles edge cases in code.

levels.1: Code does not run or fails most tests; hard to follow.
levels.2: Partially correct; noticeable bugs, awkward structure, or non-idiomatic code.
levels.3: Correct on nearly all tests; clean and readable with minor issues.
levels.4: Fully correct, clean, idiomatic, and production-quality on the first or second try.

dimensions.name: Testing & debugging
dimensions.signals: Traced through examples by hand or ran tests deliberately; considered edge cases (empty input, duplicates, negatives, bounds); debugged failures methodically instead of guessing.

levels.1: No testing; submitted without verification; random changes when tests failed.
levels.2: Ran the provided samples only; limited edge-case thinking.
levels.3: Tested meaningful edge cases and debugged failures methodically.
levels.4: Proactively designed tests that target risky logic, and caught their own bugs before running.

dimensions.name: Communication
dimensions.signals: Thought out loud; explained the plan before coding; responded well to hints and questions; was concise and structured; follow-up answers were clear and correct.

levels.1: Silent or confusing; ignored interviewer input.
levels.2: Some explanation, but disorganized or reactive; follow-up answers weak.
levels.3: Clear explanations, collaborative, and solid follow-up answers.
levels.4: Exceptionally clear and structured; led the conversation; follow-up answers were insightful.
